subject: Air-gap feasibility and private hosting: summary & next steps
messages:
From: Sara Dubois <sara.dubois@cedarcare.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cedarcare.com
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 15:06:00 +0000
Subject: Private hosting options — call recap and constraints

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side and the constraints we need Redwood to validate: 

- Regulatory driver: CedarCare handles PHI and must meet regional data residency plus evidence for audits (retention logs, immutable audit trail).
- Network isolation: preferred VPC-only deployment inside our AWS account; no general internet egress permitted from model hosts. Egress exceptions are possible but require a change control and whitelisted IPs.
- Air-gap requirement: for some workloads our compliance team wants a physically isolated environment for inference (no outbound routes) — we want to understand if Redwood can support an on-prem package or VPC-hosted nodes behind our NAT with zero egress.
- Key management: HSM-backed key storage; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) mandatory for encryption-at-rest and for model artifacts.
- Auditability: per-request audit logs, token-level retention controls, and SOC2 evidence preferred.

Attachments: cedarcare-network-sketch.pdf (simple diagram we sketched during the call).

Main asks: can you provide 1) a short feasibility note on the air-gap/on-prem option, 2) a list of technical constraints you need from our NetOps (allowed ports, IPs, cert requirements), and 3) a proposed mutual action plan with owners and timeline.

Happy to set up a separate technical deep-dive next week if needed — preferred times: Wed/Thu mornings PST.

--
Sara Dubois
Director of Infrastructure, CedarCare
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Dubois <sara.dubois@cedarcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private hosting options — call recap and constraints

Sara — thanks for the clear recap and the diagram. Appreciate the specificity; that helps a lot. Below is our working summary and immediate asks from Redwood to make a concrete plan.

Summary of constraints we heard:
- PHI + residency: must reside in US region and not be replicated outside customer VPC.
- No unrestricted egress from inference hosts; outbound only to whitelisted Redwood control-plane endpoints (if required) or 0 egress for air-gapped mode.
- BYOK via HSM for all encryption keys.
- Per-request audit logs retained for configurable retention window; ability to redact or export on-demand.

Redwood feasibility notes (short):
- Hosted Private (VPC-in-customer-account): feasible. We can run model worker nodes inside your VPC with networking restrictions and whitelisted control-plane endpoints; we can operate with minimal egress for telemetry but will document necessary flows.
- Air-gapped / On-prem package: feasible as a constrained delivery. It requires a short on-site or secure-provisioning window, operator access model, and an agreed cutover plan. Some Redwood runtime features (automatic kernel updates, telemetry) will need an offline process.

Initial technical asks for NetOps (please share):
1) Desired subnet ranges for worker nodes and NAT behavior.
2) Allowed outbound IPs (if any) for control-plane callbacks; alternatively confirm 0 egress for strict air-gap.
3) TLS termination model and whether you manage certs (we support mTLS to our control plane or customer-managed certs).
4) HSM/KMS vendor and key provisioning flow (we support AWS KMS + CloudHSM or external HSM integration).

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan:
- Redwood delivers a 2-page feasibility note and a short network-ports/IPs checklist — ETA: Tue 2027-11-30 EOD (owner: Mateo).
- CedarCare to provide NetOps contact and network ranges — ETA: Wed 2027-12-02 (owner: Sara).
- Technical deep-dive (1h) to validate the on-prem installer and audit controls — schedule after checklist exchange.

We attached a lightweight checklist and will follow up with a more detailed technical appendix for the air-gapped installer. If it's helpful I'll triage which Redwood runtime features will require offline manual steps vs. which can run normally inside a locked VPC.

Thanks — Mateo
Product Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private hosting options — call recap and constraints

Looping in ops/solutions notes. Quick bullets from infra POV after skimming Sara's sketch: 
- If they require 0 egress we should plan for an installer that runs in their environment and a secure handoff for logs (SFTP or removable media) — confirm legal constraints.
- HSM BYOK: AWS CloudHSM or Luna are okay; for external appliances we need a key-wrapping flow.
- Model updates: for air-gapped we need a signed artifact bundle + verification step. We'll need to surface timeline/ops cost — this will affect SOW.
- Networking: typical ports we need to propose: 22 (ops, optional), 443 for control-plane callbacks (if any), NTP to internal time source only, and ephemeral ports between workers. If 22/443 are blocked we need an alternative management channel.

Action for us: I'll draft an ops-impact note and a rough SOW delta (estimate) for air-gap delivery. Mateo — if you can add the functional asks (audit/retention SLAs) I'll merge.

Ben
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Dubois <sara.dubois@cedarcare.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cedarcare.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private hosting options — call recap and constraints

Thanks — this is very helpful. We're OK with Redwood preparing the feasibility note and an ops-impact / SOW delta. Confirmed next items from CedarCare: 
- NetOps contact: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@cedarcare.com> (will send full topology + ACLs by 2027-12-02).
- Compliance lead: security@cedarcare.com will share retention window requirements and audit format examples.
- Preference: initial pilot in our QA VPC (isolated) before any on-prem install.

We received the attached checklist and will review. I'll schedule the technical deep-dive for Thu 2027-12-03 16:00 PST unless you propose otherwise.

Attachments: compliance-evidence-checklist.xlsx

--
Sara Dubois
Director of Infrastructure, CedarCare
